# Assortment Box Generator – Design

Date: 2026-11-06

## Intent

A web page where the user configures a single box (or a single grid) for the SPAS system
([Small Parts Assortment System](https://www.printables.com/model/75204-small-parts-assortment-system)),
sees it in 3D and downloads an STL for a 3D printer.

**Why:** until now every variant (different size, height, moved label wedge) was generated by
hand through Claude and then checked. The generator replaces that: a new variant is a few clicks,
no tokens, no manual checking.

The boxes hold small parts (screws, wood screws, magnets…), sit on a grid in a drawer or a box,
and stack on top of each other.

## Goals

- A box of N × M modules on a 45 mm grid, any height in units, stackable, fits the grid.
- A label wedge with configurable width and an optional raised lip.
- A grid of N × M cells.
- 3D preview, STL download with one button.
- The resulting STL prints as-is (manifold, no holes, correct normals, resting on z = 0).

## Non-goals

- Laying out a whole drawer / several boxes at once – always one object, one STL.
- Inner dividers (the low wall between modules is only a by-product of the groove for the grid
  rib, see below).
- Backend, accounts, server-side storage.
- Importing or editing third-party STLs.

## Anti-goals (failure even if it "works")

- Generated boxes don't fit the grid or don't stack like the current hand-tuned versions.
- Stacked heights don't add up: 0.5 + 0.5 must be exactly as tall as 1, 1 + 0.5 as 1.5.
- The STL needs repair in the slicer.

## Constraints / decided

- **Platform:** static site, everything runs in the browser, hosted on GitHub Pages.
  Repo: https://github.com/filiphamsik/assortment-boxes (private personal project).
- **Stack:** TypeScript + Vite + three.js for the preview. Geometry is built parametrically in
  code (not by editing the reference STLs). The geometry/CSG library is left to the builder
  (candidate: `manifold-3d`, WASM – guarantees manifold output).
- **UI:** one box or one grid (mode switch), a parameter form, 3D preview (orbit with the
  mouse), a "Download STL" button. The last settings are remembered in `localStorage`.
- **File name** built from the parameters, e.g. `box_2x1_h1.5_label27.stl`, `grid_4x4.stl`.
- **Language:** everything in English – UI, code, docs, commits.

## Reference files

The geometry template is the user's own modified versions (not the Printables original):

| File (in the user's `Downloads`) | What it is |
|---|---|
| `SPAS-box_1x1.stl` | original 1×1, height 1 (35 mm) – label wedge up to the top edge (doesn't stack well) |
| `SPAS-box_2x1_smooth_v2.stl` | **template** 2×1, height 1, lowered wedge + rounded floor |
| `SPAS-box_1x1_half_stackable_v3.stl` | **template** 1×1, height 0.5 (18.5 mm), lowered wedge |
| `SPAS-grid_4x4.stl` | **template** 4×4 grid |

The builder copies them into `reference/` in the repo (they come from Printables, personal use)
and uses them to compare the generator's output.

## Geometry (measured from the reference STLs)

All dimensions in mm. Small deviations (±0.05) are rounding. **Source of truth:** where this
text and the reference STLs disagree, the measured reference sections win – except for the
deliberate changes marked "decided by user".

### Grid pitch and heights

- Pitch `G = 45`. Clearance `c = 0.4` → box outer size `N·G − c` (1×1 = 44.6; 2×1 = 89.6 – the 2×1 reference is 89.2 only because of its 44.6 foot pitch).
- Height: `H = u · 33 + 2`, where `u` = height in units (u = 1 → 35; u = 0.5 → 18.5).
  2 mm is how deep the upper box sinks into the lower one. That makes stacks add up in 33 mm
  steps.
- Range of `u`: 0.5 – 3, step 0.25. Footprint range 1–6 × 1–6 modules.

### Box – wall section (from the outer face inwards, z up)

- **Wall:** 1.0 thick, vertical from z = 3.5 to H. Outer corners in plan R = 3, inner R = 2.
- **Foot (z 0 → 3.5):** bottom face inset 1.5 from the outer face (1×1: 41.6 × 41.6), vertical
  up to z = 1.5 (small ~0.2 round at z = 0), then a ~45° chamfer outwards to full width at
  z ≈ 3.5 (smooth transition around z 2.6–3.5). The profile matches the grid rib.
- **Floor:** 1.0 thick (inner floor at z = 1.0).
- **Rounded floor (always on):** the inner floor-to-wall transition is a ~45° chamfer from the
  floor (≈ 2.4 from the wall) to the wall at z ≈ 3.5, so small parts can be scooped out. Always
  on, not a parameter (decided by user).
- **Multiple modules:** each module has its own foot, **feet are on an exact 45 mm pitch**
  (foot centre above the grid cell centre; box outline = N·45 − 0.4 centred on the same).
  The reference `2x1_smooth_v2` has feet 44.6 apart – that is a bug (zero clearance on the
  middle rib, collision from 3×1 on). Decided by user: fix to 45. Comparison with the 2×1
  reference therefore doesn't apply to foot positions (0.2 mm shift). Between the feet is a
  groove for the grid rib reaching up to z = 5.0. Inside the box this forms a low divider at
  the module boundary: a 2.0 wide wall with a flat top at z = 5.0 and vertical sides from
  z = 3.5, into which the floor chamfers of both modules run. It must not be any taller, or
  the box won't sit on the grid.
- **Top edge:** flat at z = H, no inner chamfer (a chamfer would let the upper foot sink deeper than 2 mm and break the stack heights).
- **Stacking:** the foot of the upper box (41.6 wide at the bottom) drops into the inner opening
  of the lower one (42.6) and rests on the top edge – 2 mm insertion. Nothing inside the box may
  reach into the top 3.5 mm where the foot goes (that's why the wedge is lowered).

### Label wedge

Placement: at the front wall (the wall along the X axis, −Y side), centred along it. The size
is not normalised – **N × M means "width along the label wall × depth"**, so 2×1 has the wedge
on the long wall and 1×2 on the short wall. That's how the user chooses which way the label
faces once the box is placed on the grid (decided by user: the label side must be selectable).
The UI must make this obvious (axis labels / a "label at front" marker in the preview).

- **Label surface:** horizontal at `H − 3.4` (35 → 31.6; 18.5 → 15.1), depth from the outer
  face ≈ 9.65.
- **Raised lip (optional):** U-shaped rim around the surface – 0.8–1.1 wide at the front, 1.0
  at both ends, up to `H − 3.0` (0.4 above the surface). Without the lip the whole width and
  depth (≈ 10.7 from the outer face) is flat.
- **Front face + underside:** a short vertical front face down ~2.3, then a 45° slope back to
  the wall (printable without supports).
- **Width (parameter):** outer width of the wedge including the lip (in `2x1_smooth_v2` = 27,
  flat inside 25). Slider 20 – 42.6, default 27. 42.6 = full inner width of one module (wall to
  wall on a 1×1). On boxes wider than one module the wedge is always centred and at most 42.6
  wide. Wedge ends rounded R ≈ 1 (unless it spans the full width).
- **Wedge on/off** (parameter).
- **Same label at every height (decided by user):** the label surface and lip are identical
  for every height – a 0.5 box has the same label size as a 1 box. Only the underside changes:
  at low heights the 45° slope is cut off from below where it would hit the rounded floor
  (see `half_stackable_v3`, where the slope ends at z ≈ 4 with a short flat underside).

### Grid

- Size `N·45 × M·45`, height 3.0 (no clearance – 4×4 = 180 × 180).
- Open lattice: a rib on every grid line. Inner rib: base 3.0 wide (±1.5 from the line),
  vertical up to z = 1.5, then a symmetric 45° ridge up to a peak at z = 3.0 on the line.
- Perimeter rib: half of an inner rib – outer face vertical up to z = 3.0, inner side the same
  as an inner rib (base 1.5 from the edge).
- Cells between ribs: 42 × 42 openings (the 41.6 foot sits in with 0.2 clearance per side).
- Parameters: N, M (1–10).

### Advanced (hidden, defaults from the references)

Pitch 45, clearance 0.4, wall 1.0, floor 1.0, foot height 3.5, insertion 2. Other dimensions
derive from these when changed (e.g. height step = 35 − insertion…; the builder keeps the
formulas consistent).

## Verification

- With default parameters, 2×1 / u = 1 and 1×1 / u = 0.5 / wedge width 25 must produce geometry
  matching `2x1_smooth_v2` and `half_stackable_v3` (same bounding box, sections at key planes
  within ~0.1 mm; for 2×1 except foot and divider positions, see the 45 pitch). Same for the
  4×4 grid vs `SPAS-grid_4x4`.
- Test that the feet of any N × M box have ≥ 0.2 clearance to the grid ribs on every side.
- Test that the label surface is the same size for every height.
- Output must be manifold (checked automatically).
- Heights: test that `H(a) + H(b) − 2 = H(a+b)`.

## Left to the builder

- Geometry library, code structure, UI style, deployment to GitHub Pages (GitHub Actions).
- Exact rounding of small transitions (matching the reference within tolerance is enough).
- Form defaults (suggested: 1×1, u = 1, wedge 27, lip on).
